findings.description: Upgrading changes the look for apps that pass no theme. An app that overrides the colour variables on :root (as the docs advise) now loses those overrides for the mobile cards, spinner and messages, because the wrapper redefines every variable. To stay non-breaking, the light defaults should be overridable from outside, for example by using :where() to give the defaults zero specificity and a custom-property layering scheme, or by reading app overrides first. Add a test showing that a :root override still wins.
findings.evidence: .themeRoot declares --primary-color, --text-color, --card-bg, --rt-mobile-* and the other colour variables directly on the wrapper div. A declaration on the wrapper always beats a value inherited from :root or body. Before the change these variables were declared on .responsiveTable (the <table>), so elements outside the table (mobile cards, spinner, no-more-data message) could still be themed by an app that set them on :root. docs/api.md:216 still tells apps to 'Override --primary-color at the :root level'.
findings.note: src/Styles/Theme.module.css:6 now declares the light defaults in :where(:root) (zero specificity) and the dark values in :where(.themeDark) (line 55); no colour variables are declared on the wrapper or in other CSS files, so :root/body/[data-rt-theme] overrides win. ResponsiveTable.theme.test.tsx:223 tests that overrides are not shadowed. Full jest run: 12 suites, 95 tests pass.

findings.description: The migration advice does not run as written: following the ':root' option leaves the app's colours unchanged. The note also treats a visible behaviour change as 'additive, no breaking changes'. Fix the advice, or fix the CSS so :root really works (see the R2 finding).
findings.evidence: The new v0.20.0 note says: 'If you override colour variables on the <table> element's class, move them to [data-rt-theme] or :root, since the variables are now defined on a wrapper around the table.' The wrapper itself declares every variable, so a value set on :root is shadowed by the wrapper and has no effect. Only a rule targeting [data-rt-theme] (or the wrapper class) works.
findings.note: docs/breaking-changes.md:14 now describes the zero-specificity :root defaults, so the ':root', 'body' and '[data-rt-theme]' advice works as written, and it states that the wrapper is display: contents. The note is accurate to the CSS.

findings.description: The theme change must not alter layout. The wrapper should be layout-neutral (for example display: contents, or pass-through width/height/flex) and a test should cover it. Without that, upgrading can change layout for apps that opt into nothing.
findings.evidence: Every return path of ResponsiveTable is now wrapped in a new unstyled <div> (.themeRoot has only custom properties, no display, width, height or min-height). Hosts that render the table as a direct child of a flex or grid container, or that give a parent height and rely on the table's container filling it, now see an extra block box between the parent and .tableContainer. The existing tests only assert the wrapper exists, not that layout is unchanged.
findings.note: src/Styles/Theme.module.css:47 sets .themeRoot { display: contents; } and nothing else. The test at ResponsiveTable.theme.test.tsx:217 asserts this and that the wrapper declares no colour variables.

findings.description: Use style={{ fill: 'var(--rt-nodata-icon-color, #ccc)' }} or fill="currentColor" with a colour on the parent, as the design itself described.
findings.evidence: fill="var(--rt-nodata-icon-color, #ccc)" is set as an SVG presentation attribute. Support for var() in presentation attributes is not consistent across browsers and tooling.

findings.description: Use rem for the radii in the newly added error-panel classes. The values were px before as inline styles, so this is minor.
findings.evidence: .errorPanel (padding 4rem 2rem, border-radius: 12px) and .errorRetry (border-radius: 6px) are new CSS. The 2px dashed border is fine, but the radii are in px, and the rule says px only for borders.

findings.description: R3 acceptance lines have no test that could fail: 'in the dark look no part shows the light background / dark-on-dark text', 'custom variables such as --table-header-bg still apply', and 'light look visually unchanged'. Also the edge case 'skeleton, spinner and detail rows are checked in the dark look' is only checked as 'inside the wrapper', not as dark colours. Add a test that asserts the dark and light variable sets exist and differ (for example parse Theme.module.css, check every variable the table uses is defined in both looks, and that no non-variable light hex colours remain in the module CSS used by these parts). Also assert that an app-level override of --table-header-bg is not shadowed by the wrapper.
findings.evidence: The only R3 colour test, 'the theme root uses CSS variables for default colour and background', asserts only root.style.colorScheme === 'dark'. Other R3 tests only check that skeleton/error/detail/no-data/mobile render inside the [data-rt-theme] wrapper. No test reads Theme.module.css or any computed colour. Nothing would fail if the dark variable values were missing or identical to light, if a hard-coded light colour remained, or if --table-header-bg overrides stopped applying.
findings.note: src/UI/ResponsiveTable.theme.test.tsx:160-233 adds a 'theme stylesheet' block that parses Theme.module.css. It asserts every colour variable has a light and a different dark value, and that dark defines no variable that light lacks (line 180). It checks every themed var() read by ResponsiveTable, LoadingSpinner and NoMoreDataMessage css is defined, and that the skeleton, spinner and detail-row variables exist in dark (line 192). It fails if a hard-coded hex or rgb colour remains outside var() fallbacks, shadows and keyframes (line 206). It checks the wrapper is display: contents and declares no variables (line 217). It checks light and dark variable blocks sit only on zero-specificity :where(:root) and :where(.themeDark), and that the wrapper sets no inline --table-header-bg (line 223), so an app override of --table-header-bg is not shadowed. Each of these would fail if the dark values were missing or identical to light, a light colour stayed hard-coded, or the override stopped applying. The developer reports a full suite pass (12 suites, 95 tests); I did not rerun it.

findings.description: Add an automated check of text/background variable pairs against 4.5:1 and borders/focus against 3:1 for both looks. There is no example-page check either.
findings.evidence: The developer report lists no contrast test. The accessibility NFR requires 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for focus rings and borders, checked per look. A few hard-coded colours remain in ResponsiveTable.module.css (the #ea580c and #d97706 animation colours, and the #dde3ea and #3b82f6 fallbacks).

findings.description: The R1 edge case says scroll position, selection, sort and expanded rows are preserved on theme change, and the performance NFR says scroll is not reset. The node-identity check only partly proves this. A stronger test would select a row, sort, expand and scroll before the rerender.
findings.evidence: The 'changing theme on a mounted table' test asserts that the same cell DOM node survives and that the data source is not called again. It does not set a selection, sort or expanded row, and does not set a scroll position before switching.

findings.description: The reliability NFR asks for no hydration mismatch warning with theme='system' or body.dark, and for React 18 and 19 support. Only the SSR-string path for system is proven. Light-first rendering followed by an effect makes mismatch unlikely, but it is not tested.
findings.evidence: The server-render test covers theme='system' only. There is no render with body.dark set before mount (hydration) and no hydrateRoot test. The work was done on one React version, so no React 18 and 19 matrix.

findings.description: Docs content (the examples running as written, page links, the 'default is light' and 'explicit prop wins' statements) has no automated proof. The test that tags R4 for 'explicit prop wins over body.dark' proves behaviour, not docs. A review of docs is needed. The packed-library check and release-notes size note are not evidenced.
findings.evidence: The R4 export test calls require('../index') and checks default is defined. It never checks the type's three values against the actual prop type. The packed-library check (scratch-project install, CJS and ESM import) did not run, because scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs does not exist. Neither .size-limit.json nor scripts/check-docs.mjs exists, so the size and docs checks did not run. These are accepted gaps.
